stem: Who amongst the following was the first to state that the Earth was spherical?
expl: Aristotle (384-322 BC) was a Greek philosopher and polymath. In chapter -14, Volume-2 of his book “On the Heavens” he described Earth as a spherical body. This book was translated into English by J. L. Stocks. The geographer and philosopher Ptolemy (second century A.D.) Strabo (first century BC - First century AD.) and Copernicus (15th-16th century A.D.) were the geographer/philosopher after Aristotle. Thus Aristotle was the first philosopher who argued that the Earth is spherical in shape.

stem: In completing one revolution of the sun, Earth takes approximately –
expl: The Earth takes 365.25636 days or 365 days, 6 hours, 9 minutes and 9.51 second to complete one orbit around the Sun. This period is known as ‘Solar year’. The solar year is also known as The tropical year. The tropical year is equal to 365.24 days. In the year 2000, an increase of 5 minute had been noted in comparison to other years. In this period the time was calculated to 365 days, 6 hours, 13 minutes (in place of 9 minutes), 53.26 seconds (in place of 9.51 seconds). Such a year is known as the ‘Anomalistic Year’.

stem: At which average speed the Earth revolves around the Sun?

The orbital velocity of other planets is as follows – (1) Mercury - 47.4 km/ sec (2) Venus - 35 km / sec (3) Earth - 29.8 km/ sec (4) Mars - 24.1 km/ sec (5) Jupiter - 13.1 km/ sec (6) Saturn - 9.7 km/ sec (7) Uranus - 6.8 km/ sec (8) Neptune - 5.4 km/ sec

stem:
Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below:
1. The northern end of the earth’s axis is called North Pole.
2. 45o latitude is half of the length of the equator.
3. There is parallelism of the earth's axis.
4. The earth’s speed of revolution is faster in aphelion position.
Code :
expl: The North Pole is the northernmost point of Earth i.e. northern end of the Earth’s axis is called North Pole. So, statement (1) is true. 450 latitude passes from the middle of the equator and poles. The length of the 45º parallel line is 28343.892 km, while the length of the equator is 40090.28 km. and so the 45º parallel is not half of the length of the equator and statement (2) is wrong. Parallelism of the Earth's axis means that as Earth revolves around the sun, the Earth's axis remains parallel to its previous positions. The situation of aphelion occurs on July 4, when the distance between the Sun and Earth is maximum and in the situation of aphelion the cruising speed of Earth goes slow. Thus, statement (4) is wrong.

stem: Consider one special point at the Earth’s surface (eg. City Delhi) its temperature at noon (eg. 12 O’clock) will be higher in Summer in comparison to winter because-

options.label: a
options.text: Earth is much closer to Sun in Summer in comparison to winter.

options.label: b
options.text: In winter the Sun rays falling on the Earth bends more towards the Earth’s surface in Comparison to the summer.

options.label: c
options.text: The vaporization of water happens only in winter due to environmental precipitation

options.label: d
options.text: In winters the Earth’s axis becomes more inclined towards Sun.

expl: Twice in a year on 21st March and 23rd September, Sun rays fall perpendicular to the Earth at the Equator. From 21st March to 23rd September, the Sun stands between the Equator and Tropic of Cancer. In the same period, the summer season occurs in Northern Hemisphere and winter occurs in the Southern Hemisphere. The sunrays fall in askew position in Southern Hemisphere than in Northern Hemisphere, while opposite to it from 23rd September to 21st March the Sun stands between the Equator and Tropic of Capricorn. In this period, the Sun's rays fall in a more askew position in Northern Hemisphere than in Southern Hemisphere and summer occurs in Southern Hemisphere and winter occurs in Northern Hemisphere. Due to this process, the temperature of Delhi, situated in North the Hemisphere; remains higher in summer season as compared to the winter season.

Due to the reduction in the present distance, the speed with which Earth is revolving will increase.
